record.paper_title: Selected results and open problems in a semiclassical theory of dense matter
record.context_brief: Improving the thermal equation of state
record.original_question: The proposed thermal equation of state for solids in the temperature-density plane was derived using the Bohm-Staver approximation for the equation of state through the sound speed. If that calculation is repeated with a more refined and physically accurate equation of state, how does the resulting thermal equation of state change, and does the improved treatment preserve the physically acceptable numerical values obtained in the original derivation?

evidence.quote: In the calculation which has led to the proposed form of thermal equation of state,an approximation called the "‘Bohm-Staver"’ formula was used [23].It is planned in the future to repeat this calculation,but using some more refined form of the equation of state.

artifact.category_tag: thermal equation of state for dense solids
artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a dense solid described in the temperature–density plane $(T,ho)$ within a semiclassical framework. A thermal equation of state $P_{\mathrm{th}}(T,ho)$ (the thermal contribution to the pressure) can be derived by combining the Debye-type lattice contribution with an expression for the sound speed $c_s(ho)$ in the solid. In the standard derivation one adopts the Bohm–Staver approximation
$$ c_s^{\mathrm{BS}}(ho) \;=\; \sqrt{ rac{Z\, m_e}{3\, M}}\; v_F(ho), $$
where $Z$ is the ionic charge number, $m_e$ the electron mass, $M$ the ionic mass, and $v_F(ho) = \hbar (3\pi^2 n_e)^{1/3}/m_e$ the electron Fermi velocity with electron number density $n_e = Zho/M$. This yields a closed form $P_{\mathrm{th}}^{\mathrm{BS}}(T,ho)$ whose numerical values lie within physically acceptable ranges for laboratory and stellar densities.

Replace the Bohm–Staver sound speed by a sound speed $c_s(ho)$ obtained from a more refined and physically accurate cold equation of state $P_0(ho)$ via
$$ c_s(ho)^2 \;=\;  rac{dP_0}{dho}(ho), $$
where $P_0$ incorporates exchange, correlation, and ion–ion lattice corrections beyond the free-electron Fermi gas with Bohm–Staver phonon dispersion. Carry out the same derivation of the thermal equation of state with this improved $c_s(ho)$ and determine:

(a) the explicit modified thermal equation of state $P_{\mathrm{th}}(T,ho)$ resulting from the refined sound speed;
(b) whether the numerical values of $P_{\mathrm{th}}(T,ho)$ in the physically relevant ranges of temperature and density remain within the same physically acceptable bounds as those produced by the Bohm–Staver derivation, or whether the refinement introduces qualitative or quantitative deviations.
artifact.status_search_result: No follow-up work explicitly redoing this thermal equation-of-state derivation with a refined sound speed beyond the Bohm–Staver approximation was located. The problem was posed as a future plan and its current status could not be verified from available sources.

status_evidence.snippet: It is planned in the future to repeat this calculation, but using some more refined form of the equation of state.
status_evidence.claim: The refinement is stated as a planned future task, indicating the problem was open at the time of writing.
